title: Relative flatness of finite pushforward near a singleton fibre
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $Y,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $h:Y\to S$ be a morphism, and let $\pi:Z\to Y$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and put $P=\pi_*\mathcal G$, where $P(V)=\mathcal G(\pi^{-1}V)$ with scalars restricted through $\pi^\sharp$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $P$ is quasi-coherent. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, $\pi^{-1}V$ is affine and the following conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal G|_{\pi^{-1}V}$ is flat over $S$ through $h\pi$; the $A$-module $\Gamma(\pi^{-1}V,\mathcal G)=\Gamma(V,P)$ is flat; $P|_V$ is flat over $S$ through $h$. Here relative flatness uses [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], and ordinary module flatness uses [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose now $z\in Z$, $y=\pi(z)$, and $\pi^{-1}(\{y\})=\{z\}$. Then $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S$ on some open neighbourhood of $z$ if and only if $P$ is flat over $S$ on some open neighbourhood of $y$. Also the canonical germ map $P_y\to\mathcal G_z$ is an $\mathcal O_{S,h(y)}$-linear isomorphism; in particular $P_y$ is flat over this base local ring if and only if $\mathcal G_z$ is. Stalks and their structure-map actions are as in [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. No finite generation of $\mathcal G$, finite presentation of $\pi$, affineness of $Y$ or $Z$, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $\pi$ is affine and $\pi^{-1}V$ is affine for every affine open $V$ of $Y$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] to $\pi$, $\mathcal G$ and the identity base change of $Y$: $P$ is quasi-coherent. By the definition of direct image, $\Gamma(V,P)=\Gamma(\pi^{-1}V,\mathcal G)$; its $A$-action sends $a$ to multiplication by $\pi^\sharp(h^\sharp(a))=(h\pi)^\sharp(a)$. Thus this equality identifies the two specified $A$-modules, not only their underlying groups.

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent module $F$ on a scheme $T$ over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and any affine open $W$ of $T$, [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion] identifies $A$-flatness of $F(W)$ with relative flatness of all stalks at points of $W$. Here $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)=A$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The restriction stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-stalk-iso] identifies those stalks with the stalks of $F|_W$, preserving the base action. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], $F|_W$ is again quasi-coherent, so the implications [lem-pc-relative-flat-module-stalk] and [lem-pc-relative-flat-of-stalks] apply to it and identify this stalk condition with relative flatness of $F|_W$. Apply this first to $(T,F,W)=(Z,\mathcal G,\pi^{-1}V)$ and then to $(Y,P,V)$. Step 1 gives the same $A$-module in both cases, proving all three affine conditions equivalent.

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal G|_U$ is flat over $S$ for an open neighbourhood $U$ of $z$. By [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-localization], choose an open neighbourhood $V_0$ of $y$ with $\pi^{-1}V_0\subseteq U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose $y\in V\subseteq V_0$ with $V$ affine. Every stalk on $\pi^{-1}V$ is relatively flat: use [lem-pc-relative-flat-module-stalk] on $U$ and [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-stalk-iso] for the inclusions of these opens. As $\mathcal G|_{\pi^{-1}V}$ is quasi-coherent by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], [lem-pc-relative-flat-of-stalks] makes it flat over $S$. Step 2 makes $P|_V$ flat over $S$.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, proof of (2) iff (3) and (b) iff (c), with the omitted shrinking argument supplied by Tag 05B8.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $P|_W$ is flat over $S$ on an open neighbourhood $W$ of $y$. Choose an affine $y\in V\subseteq W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Its stalks are relatively flat by [lem-pc-relative-flat-module-stalk], and the restriction stalk isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-stalk-iso] identify them with those of $P|_V$. Apply [lem-pc-relative-flat-of-stalks] to $P|_V$, which is quasi-coherent by Step 1 and clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and then Step 2: $\mathcal G|_{\pi^{-1}V}$ is flat over $S$. The open $\pi^{-1}V$ contains $z$, proving the reverse neighbourhood implication.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-localization], the canonical germ map $P_y\to\mathcal G_z$ is an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-linear isomorphism with the source stalk action through $\pi_z^\sharp$. Restrict its scalars along $h_y^\sharp:\mathcal O_{S,h(y)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. The composite scalar map is $(h\pi)_z^\sharp$, so this is exactly the requested base-linear canonical isomorphism. Flatness is invariant under this linear isomorphism: for each injective base-linear map, its two tensor maps are conjugate by tensoring with the isomorphism and its inverse; injectivity is therefore equivalent, as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].
